Verified at the data level: getSceneState(scene, 8.6).matrix.values[20..24] equals SOFTMAX.slice(20,25) exactly, with no intermediate. The timeline event at 8.4s changed from `set_values` (linear tween) to `replace_values` (discrete swap); scene-style.js/animation-scene.js's replace_values action assigns `object.values = [...event.value]` outright, so no lerp between raw score and softmax weight can ever render.

A cell now reads as this token attending to that token without cross-referencing the caption - the exact strength the reference itself was credited for in reference-notes.md.

findings.frame: none of the delivered frames - found via manual scrub diagnostics between t=5.2s and t=8.4s, outside 00/25/50/75/100
findings.observation: A heat-mapped grid/strip cell's fill can freeze at its pre-reveal 'blocked' role-tint and never update to the value-driven heat colour, even though the correct number keeps being drawn and getSceneState computes the correct value and heat token throughout. Reproduced on packages/web/src/reference-scenes.js's own matrix object: scrubbing the Animation time input gradually through several intermediate positions while a cell is still null (e.g. 0,1,2,3,4,4.4,4.8,5.0,5.2) - the natural way a human drags a range slider - then on to where its value becomes real and non-null (5.4 onward) leaves EVERY cell in the row rendering an identical, frozen `color-mix(in srgb, var(--viz-observed) ~58.5%, transparent)` fill instead of each cell's own distinct heat colour, for the remainder of the scene. Confirmed in both the dev server and a production build (npm run build + vite preview), so it is not a dev-only artifact. Confirmed NOT present when the same times are reached by discrete jumps only (the pattern the benchmark capture script and, most likely, every prior capture used) - which is why none of iteration 1's or iteration 2's official frames show it.
findings.cause: packages/web/src/AnimatedScene.jsx's grid/strip cell (~line 110-129): `style={heat ? { fill } : undefined}` and `animate={heat ? ring : { fill, ...ring }}` on the same motion.rect. While a cell is blocked (heatMode && value==null), 'fill' is driven through Framer Motion's `animate` (and springs via the `pop` transition). The moment the value first becomes real, 'fill' is dropped from `animate` and handed to the plain `style` prop instead - but if Framer Motion had already started animating 'fill' for that DOM node (i.e. the cell rendered at least one intermediate blocked frame with a live spring, not just a single jump straight past it), it continues to own and render that motion value from wherever it last was, and the plain `style.fill` this code relies on for every subsequent value never wins again for that element's lifetime.
findings.recommendation: Reusable-system fix, not a benchmark patch: a heat-mapped cell's fill must never be handed to Framer Motion's `animate` at all (put the blocked/role-tint look on `style` too, or force a fresh element identity - e.g. a `key` that changes across the blocked/revealed boundary - so no motion value survives the transition). This is general to every grid/strip cell that reveals a heat-mapped value from a blocked start, not specific to this scene; the original v1 scene had the identical reveal shape and would show the same failure under a gradual scrub.

strengths: Causal masking still reads as shape before any caption: the blank upper-right triangle is visible in 50/75/100.png.

The one row walked through end-to-end (row 4) is now fully legible end-to-end: row/column labels name every cell, the bars below repeat the same five weights with per-key labels, and the output strip's selection ring lands on the same index without disturbing its fill.

Zero bespoke code, and less incidental complexity than iteration 1: the whole case is still grid + strip + bars + arrow + text + equation, now additionally exercising rowLabels/columnLabels, heat mode, replace_values and identity - all pre-existing, generic RENDERED_TYPES fields, none scene-specific.
recommendedSystemChanges: Fix the Framer Motion animate/style handoff for heat-mapped grid/strip cells so a value-driven fill cannot get stuck on a stale STATE-driven one after a gradual reveal (see the new COORDINATION finding above - this is the blocking item for this iteration).
imitationRisk: none - different shapes (rectangles, not discs), different palette (theme CSS variables, not the reference's purple/blue/green), different layout, own wording throughout.
